judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'use its best reasonable efforts' blends two different legal standards, and the phrase 'but for the actions of the Master Servicer, the related Servicer' omits a conjunction.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with the Primary Mortgage Insurance Policy and LPMI Policy definitions, though the coverage period in the former definition is garbled.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The provision opens 'Pursuant to Sections 5.01 and 5.05' and permits withdrawal 'pursuant to Section 5.02'.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Article V of this Agreement runs only from Section 5.01 to Section 5.04, so 'Section 5.05' names a provision that does not exist.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The heading says the Trustee is to retain possession, while the text places possession and custody in the Custodians on the Trustee's behalf — heading and operative text do not match.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The Custodial Agreements and Section 2.01's delivery-to-Custodian sentence support the text rather than the heading, so the mismatch is formal but real.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'as to which no satisfactory arrangements can be made for collection of delinquent payments' is an unmeasured standard, and the operative content is then wholly deferred to 'this Agreement or the related Servicing Agreement'.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The substantive foreclosure standards live in the Servicing Agreements, which are external documents; nothing in this Agreement supplies them.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Definite in structure: fee, float income, expense-bearing and a Compensating Interest offset.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The float income is granted here and is also built into both the Master Servicing Fee and Master Servicing Compensation definitions, so the same entitlement is stated three times in different words with a risk of double counting.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'sell, any REO Property as expeditiously as possible' contains a stray comma and an unmeasured urgency standard, and 'protect and conserve, such REO Property' repeats the error.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The REMIC 'foreclosure property' constraint referenced here has to be read with Section 4.02 and the REO Property definition, which attributes acquisition to the Servicer rather than the Trust Fund.
Consistent with the Protected Account definition and Section 5.01.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The proviso refers to 'any such unreimbursed Monthly Advances', a term this Agreement never defines and which does not correspond to the 'Advances' used in the preceding clause.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Article I defines 'Advance' and 'Servicing Advances' but not 'Monthly Advances', so the proviso's referent has to be supplied from outside the instrument.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'the related Distribution Account' uses the definite article for an account of which there is only one, and the sentence lacks a comma before 'shall be deposited'.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with the Liquidation Proceeds, Protected Account and Remittance Date definitions.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The section deems non-compliance an 'Event of Default' and then declares 'This paragraph shall supersede any other provision in this Agreement or any other agreement to the contrary' — a sweeping override embedded in a reporting covenant, with an immediate termination remedy and no cure period.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Event of Default is defined by reference to Section 9.01, and Article IX contains its own notice and cure machinery for terminating the Master Servicer, so this deeming-plus-supersession paragraph cannot be harmonised with that regime.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Very long and detailed; its notable feature is the same 'This paragraph shall supersede any other provision in this Agreement or any other agreement to the contrary' override coupled with immediate termination for a reporting failure.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It again deems a reporting failure an Event of Default outside Section 9.01's definition and cure structure, and it treats the Securities Administrator's failure as a 'default' rather than an Event of Default, a distinction the Agreement does not otherwise draw.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Extremely long and procedurally dense, and it twice directs the reader to 'Section 4.18(a)(vi)(B)' for late or amended filings when the late-filing procedure is in Section 4.18(a)(v)(B) and no subsection (vi) appears.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The mis-numbered cross-reference points outside the subsections that Section 4.18(a) actually contains, and the liability carve-out here must be read with the indemnities in Section 4.18(b).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: It contains the same non-existent 'Section 4.18(a)(vi)(B)' citation, and the timetable is internally awkward: the Master Servicer must sign by the close of the 3rd Business Day while the Depositor's approval is due at the close of that same 3rd Business Day.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The cross-reference does not match the subsections of Section 4.18(a), and the signing/approval sequence has to be reconciled with the parallel but differently timed procedures in Sections 4.18(a)(i) and (iii).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: It directs the reader to 'a Sarbanes-Oxley Certification as described in Section 4.18(a)(ii)(D)' when that certification is described in subsection (a)(iii)(D) of this very provision, and it again cites the non-existent Section 4.18(a)(vi)(B); item '(IIIT)' is also mislabelled.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The internal citations do not line up with the subsections of Section 4.18 as drafted, and the provision also relies on 'the representations in Section 2.04(vi)', which is the Depositor's Exchange Act filing representation.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The opening sentence is broken: 'Additional Form 10-D Disclosure, Additional Form 10- Disclosure or any Form _8-K_ Disclosure Information (collectively, the obligation to include such Additional Information ... is subject to receipt' — the parenthetical never supplies the collective defined term, so 'Additional Disclosure' is used throughout without ever being defined.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The Additional Disclosure, Additional Form 10-D Disclosure and Additional Form 10-K Disclosure definitions in Article I all say 'As defined in Section 4.18', and this is the subsection that was to define the collective term but does not.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Long but procedurally specific; the fallback of rolling Form 8-K disclosure onto the next Form 10-D is clearly stated.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Its final sentence bars reimbursement of the Securities Administrator's Section 4.18 fees from the Trust Fund, which has to be squared with the Depositor's express responsibility for such fees in Sections 4.18(a)(i)(B), (ii)(B) and (iii)(B) and with the Section 8.05 indemnities.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The first sentence indemnifies 'the Depositor and the Master Servicer and each of its officers, directors and affiliates', where 'its' has two possible antecedents; the second sentence corrects this to 'their respective', highlighting the slip.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It overlaps with the Section 8.05 indemnity of the Trustee, Master Servicer and Securities Administrator and with the Indemnified Persons definition, which does not include the Depositor.
